the branch taken when a copy survives SIGKILL logs that no replacement is started while it lives, but reload returns into _start_or_backoff_locked at :1500 and attempts a start immediately, so the statement is untrue and no test exercises the branch (the fake process table always dies on SIGKILL).

a copy that recorded the unknown reading is treated as unrecorded and restarted, so if the service process' own identity read keeps failing while the supervisor's succeeds, each reload restarts it again; the cooldown the sentinel is meant to give covers only a failing read in the supervisor, not one in the copy.
